Definition: from G4215 and a derivative of G5409; river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream:--carried away of the flood.
BiblicalUsage: Potamophoretos means carried away by a flood, river-borne. John uses it once: the serpent casts water as a flood after the woman, to carry her away, but the earth opens its mouth and swallows the flood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the flood always fails against the woman God keeps, because the earth itself answers to him.
